rules.why: The switch is the native checkbox with role="switch": the browser keeps the state, the keyboard and the announcement in sync.
Only the native input is a switch; any other element with role="switch" needs JS the AL does not ship.
The state comes from checked; a parallel aria-checked or aria-pressed drifts from what the screen paints.
The visible label is the accessible name, and it pays for the 1.47:1 border and the 1.96:1 thumb.
With a visible label, aria-label or aria-labelledby makes what is read differ from what is seen.
The switch has no error state and is never required: its effect is immediate.
The thumb is paint; the input already announces the state.
